```{r setup}
# Everything shown on the slides comes from results/, written by ./run_all.sh.
# Paths are relative to this file's folder (slides/).
res <- "../results"
cfg <- local({
  lines <- readLines("../config/config.sh")
  m <- regmatches(lines, regexec("^([A-Z0-9_]+)=\\$\\{\\1:-([^}]*)\\}", lines, perl = TRUE))
  m <- m[lengths(m) == 3]
  v <- setNames(vapply(m, `[`, "", 3), vapply(m, `[`, "", 2))
  env <- Sys.getenv(names(v), unset = "")
  v[nzchar(env)] <- env[nzchar(env)]
  as.list(v)
})
padj_cut <- as.numeric(cfg$PADJ_CUTOFF)
lfc_cut <- as.numeric(cfg$LFC_CUTOFF)
have <- function(p) file.exists(file.path(res, p))
# fig("folder/file.png"): the image, or a visible note when that step has not produced it
fig <- function(p, attr = ".r-stretch") {
  if (have(p)) sprintf("![](%s){%s}", file.path(res, p), attr)
  else sprintf("*[not generated yet: results/%s]*", p)
}
big <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)

samples <- read.delim(file.path("..", cfg$SAMPLES), comment.char = "#")
de <- read.delim(file.path(res, "downstream/2_dea/deseq2_all_genes.tsv"))
n_tested <- nrow(de)
summary_txt <- readLines(file.path(res, "downstream/2_dea/summary.txt"))
n_sig <- as.integer(sub(".*: ([0-9]+) .*", "\\1", grep("^Genes with padj", summary_txt, value = TRUE)))
n_up <- sum(de$direction == "up"); n_down <- sum(de$direction == "down")

funnel <- if (have("downstream/0_upstream/01_read_funnel.tsv"))
  read.delim(file.path(res, "downstream/0_upstream/01_read_funnel.tsv"))
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * median(x / funnel$sequenced))
depth_file <- file.path(res, "downstream/2_dea/02_depth_check.txt")
depth_line <- if (file.exists(depth_file)) {
  d <- readLines(depth_file)
  full <- as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", d[2])); found <- as.numeric(sub(".*: ([0-9]+).*", "\\1", d[3]))
  sprintf("the full data found %.0f× more significant genes.", full / found)
} else "deeper data finds more genes."
norm_info <- if (have("downstream/1_eda/02_normalization.tsv"))
  read.delim(file.path(res, "downstream/1_eda/02_normalization.tsv"))
own_sf <- if (have("downstream/1_eda/01_library_sizes.tsv"))
  range(read.delim(file.path(res, "downstream/1_eda/01_library_sizes.tsv"))$size_factor)
norm_note <- if (!is.null(norm_info) && cfg$COUNTS_SOURCE == "pipeline" &&
                 grepl("^published", norm_info$counts[1]) && !is.null(own_sf))
  sprintf("If asked why not our own counts: the 2 M-read subsets have equal depths (size factors
%.2f to %.2f), so there is nothing to correct; the plot uses the published full-depth counts.",
          own_sf[1], own_sf[2]) else ""
depth_range <- if (!is.null(norm_info))
  sprintf(" (here %.0f–%.0f M reads)", min(norm_info$million_reads), max(norm_info$million_reads)) else ""
edger_caption <- if (have("downstream/2_dea/01_deseq2_vs_edger_overlap.tsv")) {
  ov <- read.delim(file.path(res, "downstream/2_dea/01_deseq2_vs_edger_overlap.tsv"))
  n_ov <- setNames(ov$genes, ov$called_by)
  sprintf("Same fold changes, different strictness. Significant genes: DESeq2 %s, edgeR %s, in both %s%s.",
          big(n_ov[["both"]] + n_ov[["DESeq2 only"]]), big(n_ov[["both"]] + n_ov[["edgeR only"]]),
          big(n_ov[["both"]]), if (n_ov[["DESeq2 only"]] == 0) " (every DESeq2 gene)" else "")
} else ""
depth_x <- if (file.exists(depth_file)) sub(".*about ([0-9]+)x.*", "\\1", readLines(depth_file)[2]) else "?"
depth_r <- if (file.exists(depth_file)) sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", readLines(depth_file)[4]))) else "?"
pathview_png <- list.files(file.path(res, "downstream/7_enriched_path"), pattern = "pathview\\.png$")[1]
```

## The question {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**What does dexamethasone do to airway smooth muscle cells?**

- Dexamethasone: a glucocorticoid, the standard anti-inflammatory drug in asthma
- Airway smooth muscle (ASM) cells from **4 donors**
- Each donor's cells: **untreated** and **treated** (1 µM, 18 h)
- Total: 8 RNA-seq samples, paired-end Illumina reads

<br>

::: {.muted .small}
Himes *et al.* (2014) *PLoS One* 9:e99625, GEO GSE52778.
Bioconductor package: `airway`.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(sample = samples$sample, donor = samples$batch, condition = samples$condition))
```
:::
::::

## The road map

| | Step | Tool | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| **upstream** | 0. get the reference (once) | `curl` from HISAT2 and Ensembl | genome index, gene annotation |
| | 1. get reads | `curl` from ENA | FASTQ |
| | 2. quality control | FastQC, MultiQC | HTML reports |
| | 3. trim | Trimmomatic | cleaner FASTQ |
| | 4. align to the genome | HISAT2, samtools | BAM |
| | 5. count reads per gene | featureCounts (or Salmon) | **count matrix** |
| **downstream** | 6. explore | DESeq2 (VST, PCA) | plots |
| | 7. differential expression | DESeq2 (+ edgeR) | gene table |
| | 8. interpretation | clusterProfiler, DOSE, ReactomePA | GO, pathways, diseases |

::: {.small .muted}
Every step is one script in the repository; `./run_all.sh` runs all of them and builds these slides.
:::

# Upstream: from reads to counts

## A read in a FASTQ file

```{r}
first_read <- c("@SRR1039508.1 HWI-ST177:290:C0TECACXX:1:1101:1225:2130/1",
                "CATTGCTGATACCAANNNNNNNNGCATTCCTCAAGGTCTTCCTCCTTCCCTTACGGAATTACA",
                "+",
                "HJJJJJJJJJJJJJJ########00?GHIJJJJJJJIJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJJHHHFFFFFD")
```

::: {.qual}
`r first_read[1]`  ← read name<br>
`r first_read[2]`  ← the bases<br>
`r first_read[3]`<br>
`r first_read[4]`  ← one quality letter per base
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
| Part of the name | Meaning |
|------|------------------|
| `SRR1039508` | run in the public archive (SRA/ENA): donor N61311, untreated |
| `.1` | pair number in the file: the first read pair |
| `HWI-ST177` | instrument ID (an Illumina HiSeq 2000) |
| `290` | run number on that instrument |
| `C0TECACXX` | flow cell ID |
| `1` | lane on the flow cell |
| `1101` | tile: one imaged patch of the lane |
| `1225:2130` | X and Y position of the cluster on the tile |
| `/1` | read 1 of the pair; its mate in the R2 file ends in `/2` |
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Quality letter = Phred score **Q** = −10 · log~10~(error probability)
- `J` = Q41 (1 error in ~12,000), `#` = Q2: the 8 `N`s were unreadable
- This is read 1 of the first sample, not hand-picked: 8 bases unreadable. Rare (0.4% of reads), but QC and trimming exist for exactly this: trimming dropped this read.
:::
::::

## Get the reads, check their quality

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
```bash
# 1. get reads: stream the run's 2 files from ENA,
#    keep the first 2 M reads (4 lines per read)
curl -sL $URL_R1 | gzip -dc | head -n 8000000 | gzip > R1.fq.gz
curl -sL $URL_R2 | gzip -dc | head -n 8000000 | gzip > R2.fq.gz
```
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
```bash
# 2. quality control: one report
#    per file, MultiQC merges them
fastqc R1.fq.gz R2.fq.gz
multiqc .
```
:::
::::

`r fig("upstream/multiqc/multiqc_report_plots/png/fastqc_per_base_sequence_quality_plot.png")`

::: {.small .muted}
Mean quality along the read, every FASTQ file (raw and trimmed). Green = good. The 16 ENA URLs are in `config/samples.tsv`.
:::

## Trim, align, count

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```bash
# 0. once: index the human genome (GRCh38)
#    (we download this index prebuilt: 8 files, 4 GB)
hisat2-build genome.fa grch38/genome

# 3. trim: cut low-quality ends, drop short reads
trimmomatic PE R1.fq.gz R2.fq.gz \
  R1_trimmed.fq.gz R1_unpaired.fq.gz \
  R2_trimmed.fq.gz R2_unpaired.fq.gz \
  ILLUMINACLIP:TruSeq3-PE-2.fa:2:30:10:2:True \
  SLIDINGWINDOW:4:20 MINLEN:25

# 4. align (splice-aware), sort, index
hisat2 -x grch38/genome \
  -1 R1_trimmed.fq.gz -2 R2_trimmed.fq.gz |
  samtools sort -o sample.bam
samtools index sample.bam

# 5. count read pairs per gene
featureCounts -p --countReadPairs -s 0 \
  -a Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.gtf.gz \
  -o counts.txt *.bam
```

::: {.small .muted}
`grch38/genome` = the index files' shared name (`genome.1.ht2` ... `genome.8.ht2`). The GTF is
Ensembl's gene annotation: where each gene and exon lies on the genome.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="52%"}
`r fig("downstream/0_upstream/01_read_funnel.png", 'width="100%"')`

::: {.small}
`r if (!is.null(funnel)) sprintf("Of %s read pairs per sample, %s survive trimming, %s align, %s land in a gene.", big(median(funnel$sequenced)), pct(funnel$after_trimming), pct(funnel$aligned), pct(funnel$assigned_to_gene))`
:::
:::

## The count matrix, and a second route

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
counts_file <- file.path(res, "upstream/featureCounts/gene_counts.tsv")
if (file.exists(counts_file)) {
  counts <- read.delim(counts_file, check.names = FALSE)
  show <- c(head(de$gene_id[!is.na(de$symbol)], 4), de$gene_id[which(de$symbol == "ACTB")])
  m <- counts[match(show, counts$gene_id), 2:5]     # first two donors; all 8 samples are in the file
  rownames(m) <- de$symbol[match(show, de$gene_id)]
  cond <- samples$condition[match(names(m), samples$sample)]
  names(m) <- paste0(ifelse(cond == cfg$REFERENCE_LEVEL, "untreated", "treated"), "<br>",
                     samples$batch[match(names(m), samples$sample)])
  knitr::kable(m, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), escape = FALSE)
}
```
::: {.small}
One row per gene (`r big(nrow(counts))` in the annotation), one column per sample (2 of 4 donors shown):
**raw counts**, not normalized. This table is the input for everything downstream.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
`r fig("downstream/0_upstream/03_featurecounts_vs_salmon.png", 'width="100%"')`

::: {.small}
**Salmon** skips alignment: it maps reads to transcript sequences and estimates counts in seconds.
:::
:::
::::

## Choosing the upstream tools

| Tool | What it does | Pick it when | Trade-off |
|-----------|--------------|----------------|------------|
| **STAR** | aligns reads to the genome, across splice junctions | you need new splice junctions, fusions or variants; large projects (ENCODE, TCGA) | ~32 GB RAM for a human genome |
| **HISAT2** (used here) | the same job, with a compact index | memory is limited: a laptop, a course, a small server | ~8 GB RAM |
| **featureCounts** (used here) or HTSeq-count | counts aligned reads per gene, from the BAM | gene-level differential expression; simple and transparent | reads that fit several genes are dropped |
| **Salmon** or kallisto (Salmon used here as a check) | skips the genome: matches reads to known transcripts and estimates counts | you only need expression: many samples, little time, isoforms | no BAM to look at; finds no new genes, junctions or variants |

::: {.callout-box}
Need to **see the reads** or find something new (coverage, new splice junctions, variants)? Align.
Need **counts**, even per known isoform? Salmon is enough. Many pipelines do both: nf-core/rnaseq aligns with STAR and counts with Salmon.
:::

::: {.small .muted}
Here: HISAT2 + featureCounts fit a laptop and give the BAM behind the coverage plot; Salmon checks the counts.
:::

# Downstream: from counts to genes

## Normalization: comparing samples fairly

`r fig("downstream/1_eda/02_normalization.png")`

::: {.small .muted}
Depths differ`r depth_range`. **Size factor** = median of a sample's ratios to the gene averages;
DESeq2 divides by it. Most genes don't change between samples, so how far a sample's typical gene
sits from average tells us its sequencing depth, and we divide that out.
:::

## Do the samples group by treatment?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
`r fig("downstream/1_eda/03_pca.png", 'width="100%"')`
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
`r fig("downstream/1_eda/04_sample_distances.png", 'width="100%"')`
:::
::::

::: {.small}
PC1 = treatment. PC2 = one donor that differs from the others.
:::

## The model: DESeq2

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
```r
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = counts,
  colData   = samples,
  design    = ~ batch + condition)
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds, contrast =
  c("condition", "dexamethasone", "untreated"))
```

::: {.small}
- Counts ~ negative binomial (overdispersed Poisson)
- `~ batch + condition`: compare treated vs. untreated **within each donor**
- `r big(n_tested)` genes tested, **`r big(n_sig)`** with FDR < `r padj_cut`
- `r sprintf("<span class='up'>%d up</span>, <span class='down'>%d down</span> by more than %g-fold", n_up, n_down, 2^lfc_cut)`
:::
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
top <- head(de[!is.na(de$symbol), c("symbol", "baseMean", "log2FC_shrunk", "padj")], 10)
top$padj <- formatC(top$padj, format = "e", digits = 1)
names(top) <- c("gene", "mean count", "log2 FC", "adj. p")
knitr::kable(top, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```
:::

# From genes to biology

## Two ways to ask "what do these genes do?"

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Over-representation (ORA)

1. Take the significant genes
2. For each gene set (GO term, pathway): more of its genes in the list than expected?
3. Hypergeometric / Fisher's test against the **universe** of tested genes

```r
enrichGO(sig_genes, universe = tested_genes,
         OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = "BP")
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Gene set enrichment (GSEA)

1. Rank **all** genes from most up to most down
2. Do a set's genes cluster at the top or bottom?
3. No cutoff needed; catches many small shifts

```r
gseGO(ranked_genes,
      OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, ont = "BP")
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-box}
Same idea for every database: GO (functions), KEGG / Reactome / WikiPathways (pathways),
Disease Ontology (diseases).
:::

## Take-home messages

- **Design decides everything**: replicates, pairing, balanced batches. No pipeline fixes a confounded design.
- **Look before you test**: QC reports, PCA, sample distances.
- **Raw counts in, normalization inside the model**; account for batch / donor in the design.
- **FDR, not p-value**; shrunken fold changes for ranking and plots.
- **Enrichment is a summary, not a proof**: right universe, many redundant terms, database bias.
- **Depth buys power**: `r big(as.numeric(cfg$N_READS))` read pairs per sample found the strong effects; `r depth_line`

## Run it yourself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mortezasabri/rnaseq-workshop.git && cd rnaseq-workshop
micromamba env create -f environment.yml && micromamba activate rnaseq-workshop
./run_all.sh --dry-run     # checks tools, packages, sample sheet
./run_all.sh               # FASTQ -> results -> these slides (~15 min + one-time 6 GB download)

COUNTS_SOURCE=airway ./run_all.sh downstream   # laptop-only: skip upstream, use published counts
```

::: {.small}
- One script per step: `upstream/01_download.sh` … `downstream/12_ReactomePA.R`
- Own data: copy `config/samples.template.tsv`, fill it in, `SAMPLES=config/my_samples.tsv ./run_all.sh`
- Further reading: the DESeq2 RNA-seq workflow (`rnaseqGene`), the clusterProfiler book
:::
